summary: Silverfort Advanced: MFA, service account protection and identity threat detection with the Authentication Firewall.
value: Password and Kerberos ticket theft and moving around under someone else’s name are visible and can be blocked.
Each account may sign in only where its work requires.
Service accounts and legacy systems are protected without agents.
simple: Account protection built right into the sign-in process (Active Directory, cloud directories, other authentication systems) — without agents or changes to applications, in on-premises, cloud and hybrid environments. Builds a single inventory and graph of all accounts — human and machine — and their permissions. Finds weak spots: hidden administrators, outdated and abandoned accounts, insecure settings, outdated protocols (ISPM). Extends multi-factor authentication (MFA) to things that usually don’t support it: legacy and custom applications, the command line, OT equipment, local Windows sign-ins. Finds all service accounts and AI agents, identifies their owners and usual routes, and “fences them in”: lets them sign in only where they normally go and blocks deviations (NHI Security, AI Agent Security). Checks every sign-in attempt against segmentation rules and blocks risky ones — stops lateral movement and ransomware spread, and has a “freeze” mode during an attack (Authentication Firewall, part of the ITDR class). Detects attacks on accounts in real time — password guessing and spraying, Pass-the-Hash, Pass-the-Ticket, Kerberoasting, DCSync — and immediately blocks the sign-in, requires MFA or ends the session; passes events to XDR and SIEM (ITDR). The set of modules may differ for on-premises, cloud or hybrid environments.
classification: The Authentication Firewall (access segmentation) is part of ITDR (author’s decision); ITDR gained D3-ST and D3-UAP.
